title: Contract renewal notifications and exit cost models
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document standardizes Redwood Inference’s contract renewal notification timelines, escalation procedures, and a repeatable model for calculating exit costs and revenue recognition impacts when contracts are amended, renewed, or terminated. It is intended for use by Finance, Legal, Sales Ops, and Procurement.

Scope:
- Applies to customer, partner, and vendor contracts where Redwood is party to: hosted API, Dedicated/Reserved capacity, Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), or professional services engagements.
- Excludes purely internal vendor subscription renewals under $5k/year unless aggregated by procurement.

Definitions
- Renewal notice window: the primary set of calendar days before contract end that triggers outreach (90/60/30).
- Exit cost: cumulative spend and non-recurring charges Redwood expects to incur or forego when a contract is terminated or not renewed (see components below).
- Revenue impact window: accounting period(s) affected when a contract is modified or terminated.

Principles
1) Predictability: teams must provide standardized notices to downstream functions with consistent timelines and templates.
2) Transparency: all commercial changes must surface to RevRec, Billing, and Customer Success before signature.
3) Minimal disruption: prioritize migration/transition plans for customer-facing contracts affecting production (Dedicated/Private).

Roles and ownership
- Legal (Contracts Manager): final approval of contract language, templates, and exit clauses.
- Finance (RevRec Lead): certifies revenue accounting treatment, calculates projected revenue impact and exit cost.
- Sales Ops/Account Exec: owns customer notifications and renewal commercial terms.
- Procurement: coordinates vendor renewals and cost-avoidance analysis.
- Customer Success: executes migration/runbook with the customer for any termination scenarios.

Renewal notification timeline (standardized)
| Days before EoC | Action | Owner | System/Artifact |
|------------------|--------|-------|-----------------|
| 90 | Renewal intent email + internal renewal review kickoff | Sales Ops | CRM opportunity tag: renewal_90d |
| 60 | Pricing proposal & risk checklist to Legal + Finance | Sales Ops | Contract request (Confluence ticket + DocuSign draft) |
| 30 | Final commercial terms, RevRec signoff, procurement review (if applicable) | Legal/Finance/Procurement | Contract package in shared folder (s3) |
| 14 | Exec escalation if no agreement or if exit likely | Head of Revenue / Legal Counsel | Exec escalation email + brief |

Detailed procedures
1) 90-day step: Sales Ops opens renewal opportunity and sets the CRM stage to renewal_90d. Account owner must attach the current signed contract and note any historical amendments. If model/hosting changes are proposed (e.g., migrating from hosted to Dedicated), flag for Private Deployments team.
2) 60-day step: Finance runs an preliminary RevRec impact run using the Renewal Impact Template (see Appendix A). Finance returns a memo if there is an expected revenue timing change greater than $50k or >10% of ARR contribution.
3) 30-day step: Legal reviews proposed amendments and updates escape/exit terms. Any non-standard termination or extended notice (>120 days or <30 days) must be routed to Legal Director.
4) 14-day step: If there is unresolved commercial negotiation or the customer signals termination, Customer Success prepares transition runbook (data export, KV cache wipe procedures for Private deployments) and Finance prepares final exit cost estimate.

Exit cost model (components and sample calculation)
Use the following components to compute a conservative exit cost estimate. Each component should be one line item in the Exit Cost Worksheet:
- Unamortized implementation fees: capitalized onboarding or customization fees not yet recognized.
- Remaining committed infrastructure charges: GPU cloud reservations, Dedicated pool costs allocated to customer commit period (prorated).
- Early termination fees (if contract includes) or projected churn-related revenue loss over a 12-month horizon (whichever higher).
- Data migration and engineering runbook labor: estimated FTE-hours * fully loaded rate. Default: $200/hr for eng, $120/hr for CS, $80/hr for support.
- Third-party transfer costs: licenses, third-party tool termination penalties.
- Contract exit admin: Legal and procurement review costs (standard flat $2,000 unless bespoke).

Sample ASCII table (example estimate):
| Component | Basis | Amount (USD) |
|-------------------------------|--------------------------|---------------:|
| Unamortized onboarding | Remaining 6 months amortization | 18,000 |
| Committed infra (prorated) | 2 GPUs reserved, 3 months leftover | 24,000 |
| Migration engineering | 40 hours * $200/hr | 8,000 |
| Third-party transfer | License termination | 1,500 |
| Admin/legal review | Flat rate | 2,000 |
| TOTAL | | 53,500 |

Accounting and RevRec guidance
- Small amendments that do not change standalone selling price (SSP) or contract term: treat as modification under ASC 606 guidance; Finance to confirm no change to revenue recognition schedule.
- Material changes (>= $50k impact or change to performance obligations): Finance will re-evaluate the contract and determine whether to prospectively recognize or to remeasure the transaction price.
- Early terminations: recognize any remaining defeRRed revenue consistent with policy; where termination includes exit fee, defer recognition until collectibility is probable.
- Notification: RevRec Lead must produce a one-page accounting memo for legal signature when the revenue impact exceeds $50k or the term change > 3 months.

Procurement coordination checklist (vendor renewals)
- Confirm owner and budget center.
- Gather current usage and forecast for next 12 months.
- Evaluate right-sizing options (paused resources, smaller instance types, quantized model variants).
- If canceling: estimate termination costs per model above and compare to cost of continued renewal.

Contract amendment and approval workflow (steps)
1) Draft amendment in template (Legal provides marked-up clause set).
2) Sales Ops attaches approved pricing in CRM and notifies Finance.
3) Finance runs RevRec impact and signs off or escalates.
4) Legal signs and circulates for signature (DocuSign).
5) Procurement (vendor) or Billing (customer) records routing codes and updates chargeback mapping.

Escalation and exec triggers
- Automatic exec review when estimated exit cost > $100k or when renewal impacts > 10% of the customer’s ARR contribution.
- If negotiation extends beyond 14 days before EoC with no signed amendment, trigger Head of Revenue + Legal Director for decision (renew, transition, or accept termination).

Templates and examples
1) 90-day renewal notification (email subject + body):
Subject: Renewal notice — [Account] contract ends [YYYY-MM-DD] — action requested
Body: Hello [Name], our records show your contract for [Product/Service] is scheduled to end on [date]. We’d like to discuss the renewal options and any changes to usage or deployment. Please book time here: [calendar link].
2) 30-day RevRec memo example: one paragraph summarizing change in timing and dollar impact with table of line items (see Appendix A).

Operational controls and SLOs
- CRM tagging: 100% of contracts with EoC within 120 days must have CRM renewal tag set. (Owner: Sales Ops)
- RevRec signoff SLA: Finance will provide preliminary RevRec impact within 5 business days of request. (Owner: Finance)
- Legal turnaround SLA for standard amendments: 7 business days. (Owner: Legal)

Appendices
Appendix A — Minimum fields required in Renewal Impact Template:
- Contract ID, Customer name, Contract start/end, Current ARR, Proposed ARR, Change in term (months), One-time credits/fees, Unamortized onboarding balance, Estimated infra commitments, Estimated engineering hours, RevRec recommendation, Finance approver initials.

Appendix B — Sample SQL to estimate remaining infra commitment (example):
SELECT contract_id, SUM(prorated_monthly_commit) AS remaining_commit
FROM infra_commitments
WHERE contract_id = 'C-12345' AND end_date > CURRENT_DATE;
